newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fletcher says testing fifth Brunei well.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher says testing fifth Brunei well.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Energy said on Wednesday that Maharaja Lela-3 (ML-3), the fifth well in Brunei's Maharaja Lela gas/condensate field area, was currently being drill stem-tested.
It said the first of three tests was in progress in the J1 sands objective at an along hole depth of 3,713.75 metres to 3,720.75 metres, and 3,723.75 metres to 3,753.75 metres.
"Gas flows have been recorded and testing is continuing with a pressure build-up survey," the company said.
The most recent test produced at a rate of 29.1 million cubic feet of gas and 444 barrels of condensate per day at 2,314 psi, flowing wellhead pressure through a 3/4 inch choke.
On completion of testing in the J1 sands, two further tests are programmed.
Fletcher Challenge Energy, through its operating company in Brunei (Fletcher Challenge Petroleum Borneo), farmed into PMA Block B in February 1996 and holds a 35 percent interest.
Partners in the venture are Elf Petroleum Asia BV, the operator, with 37.5 percent; and Jasra International Petroleum Sendirian Berhad and other Bruneian interests with 27.5 percent.
